questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A person standing on a weighing machine inside a lift whose cable has snapped, so that the lift falls freely, will see a reading of:
questions.explanation: In free fall a = g, so the normal reaction N = m(g - a) becomes zero. The person has not lost mass or weight; the support force is simply gone.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 4: Laws of Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The momentum p of a body of mass m having kinetic energy E is given by:
questions.explanation: From E = p²/2m we get p = √(2mE). So of two bodies with the same kinetic energy, the heavier one carries the greater momentum.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 5: Work, Energy and Power

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question: The perpendicular axis theorem, Iz = Ix + Iy, can be applied only to:
options: A planar lamina, with the three axes mutually perpendicular and the first normal to its plane
A body rotating about its centre of mass only
questions.explanation: The theorem holds for a flat lamina because the mass has no extension along the z direction. The parallel axis theorem is the one that applies to bodies of any shape.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 6: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question: An electrophile is best defined as a species that is:
options: Electron rich and attacks positive centres
Electron deficient and attacks electron rich centres
questions.explanation: An electrophile may be a cation such as NO₂⁺ or a neutral electron deficient molecule such as BF₃ or SO₃. A nucleophile is the electron rich partner.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 8: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of an alkyl chloride with sodium iodide in dry acetone to give the alkyl iodide is known as the:
questions.explanation: The reaction is driven forward because sodium chloride is insoluble in acetone and precipitates out. The Swarts reaction uses metallic fluorides to make alkyl fluorides.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 6: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The heat change measured in a bomb calorimeter, in which the volume is kept constant, gives:
options: ΔU, since no pressure-volume work is done
questions.explanation: At constant volume W = 0, so qv = ΔU. ΔH is then obtained using ΔH = ΔU + ΔngRT, which is why combustion data must be converted before use.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The nucleolus present inside the nucleus is the site of:
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is not membrane bound and is larger in cells that make a lot of protein, because it assembles the rRNA that ribosomes are built from.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 8: Cell: The Unit of Life

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Kranz anatomy, in which large bundle sheath cells surround the vascular bundles, is characteristic of:
options: C₄ plants such as maize and sugarcane
questions.explanation: The bundle sheath cells are rich in chloroplasts, have thick impervious walls and no intercellular spaces, which keeps the CO₂ concentration around RuBisCO high.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 11: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: A sarcomere, the functional unit of a striated muscle fibre, is the portion of a myofibril between:
options: The M line and the Z line
questions.explanation: Each sarcomere has a central A band of myosin with half an I band of actin at either end, and contraction shortens the sarcomere by pulling the Z lines closer.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 17: Locomotion and Movement

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Ascariasis in humans is caused by a:
questions.explanation: The intestinal roundworm spreads through water, vegetables and soil contaminated with its eggs, and causes internal bleeding, fever and blockage of the intestine.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease
